content.title: How to watch Warriors vs Suns Play-In game without cable tonight
content.text: The Warriors face the Suns in a win-or-go-home Play-In game with a playoff spot on the line.Billy CaddenThe Warriors are still alive, and they’re bringing plenty of momentum into Friday night’s Play-In showdown against the Suns. After trailing most of the game against the Clippers on Wednesday, Golden State pulled off a stunning 126-121 comeback win, erasing a 13-point 4th-quarter deficit behind a vintage performance from Steph Curry and Al Horford. The two oldest players on the court caught fire late, knocking down clutch threes to flip the game, while Draymond Green anchored the defense with key stops on Kawhi Leonard in the final minutes. It was everything fans have seen time and time again over the years — Steph leading the charge with 35 points and timely shooting, and Draymond making game-changing plays when it mattered most.Now, they’ll need to do it all over again against Devin Booker and the Suns, with even higher stakes. Friday’s game is another win-or-go-home scenario, with the winner advancing to face the Thunder in the first round and the loser heading home for the offseason. Phoenix enters as a slight 3-point favorite, but as Wednesday proved, the Warriors are far from done. If Curry finds his rhythm, it only takes a few deep threes to swing everything. With the season on the line and a playoff berth within reach, this is another must-watch night for Warriors fans.The Warriors vs Suns Play-In game tips off Friday night at 7:00 p.m. PDT, and fans everywhere can catch all the action exclusively on Prime Video.When is Warriors vs Suns? What: Golden State Warriors @ Phoenix Suns — Play-In Tournament Game When: Friday, April 17, 2026, at 7:00 p.m. PDT Where: Mortgage Matchup Center, Phoenix, AZ TV: Prime Video How to stream the Warriors vs Suns Play-In game without cableAll six games of the Play-In tournament, including the Warriors vs Suns game, air exclusively on Amazon Prime Video this year. So you won’t be able to watch the Dubs on Friday night with any other streaming platform, cable TV, or even on NBC Sports Bay Area. To tune into this matchup, you need to sign up for Amazon Prime to get access to Prime Video.If the Warriors beat the Suns, you’ll need Prime to catch at least one of their games against the Thunder, not to mention one-third of all other playoff games across the league during the first two rounds. So while it might be a little frustrating to need yet another streaming service to watch the NBA, Prime Video is pretty essential for fans at this point. That said, the platform is only airing games during the Play-In and the first two rounds, so you can take advantage of Amazon’s 30-day free trial and watch nearly every game on Prime without paying a dime.Prime Video might not offer as much live TV as other streaming services, but for just $14.99/month, an Amazon Prime membership remains one of the best values out there. In addition to being able to watch the Warriors-Suns game and about a third of the first and second round games this postseason, you’ll also get complete access to plenty of other Prime member-exclusive benefits: Free delivery on many Amazon purchases Free GrubHub+ membership Amazon key for safer, in-garage delivery Prime Day and Prime-member exclusive deals Amazon music unlimited April 17, 2026Andrew Koopman is a freelance writer who's been producing content since 2020. If he's not writing, Andrew is almost certainly watching sports (go Warriors!) or planning his next adventure as he attempts to visit all 50 states in the next few years.
